prompt:
Redraw this photograph from scratch as an original 1963 Roy Lichtenstein romance-comic panel. This is NOT a filter, a recolor, or a halftone overlay applied to a photo - it is a complete hand re-illustration. Discard the photograph's lighting, shadows, skin texture, film grain, color grade and depth of field entirely. Nothing photographic may survive into the output.

KEEP FROM THE SOURCE ONLY: head angle and tilt, gaze direction, the silhouette and mass of the hair, mouth open or closed, and the broad proportion of the face. The subject should be recognizable the way a comic caricature is recognizable - through pose and gross feature placement, NOT through rendered likeness. Do not attempt a faithful portrait.

REBUILD THE FACE WITH LICHTENSTEIN COMIC CONSTRUCTION:
- Skin: ONE flat field of uniform mechanical Ben-Day dots in classic red at coarse scale and balanced 50 percent coverage, over pure white. Absolutely no modeling - no cheekbones, no nose shadow, no jaw shading, no blush, no contouring. The face reads completely FLAT.
- Eyes: enlarged well beyond life size, almond shaped, pure white sclera. Iris a perfect circle with heavy black outline and a solid black pupil. Upper lid a thick solid black band. Lashes as a row of individual black spikes.
- Eyebrows: solid tapered black shapes with a high dramatic arch. No individual hairs.
- Nose: reduced to TWO OR THREE thin black contour lines only. No nostril mass, no bridge, no tip shading. This is the single most important simplification - a photographic nose instantly breaks the style.
- Lips: flat saturated red with a hard black outline and one bold white specular streak. Teeth as flat white shapes divided by thin black lines.
- Hair: rebuilt as sweeping calligraphic ribbons of flat solid jet black with bold white highlight ribbons, each mass bounded by thick black contour with long black strand lines flowing inside. Never individual realistic strands.
- Clothing and objects: flat unmodulated color blocks with thick black outlines. No fabric texture; folds reduced to two or three bold black lines.
- Background: flat the white flowers redrawn as flat white petal shapes with thick black outlines on a flat cyan field. No depth, no perspective, no photographic detail.

LINE: every form bounded by confident black ink contour at heavy bold contour, uniform width, hand-inked rather than vector-crisp.
EXPRESSION: push to full melodrama - comic melodrama, not the photograph's subtle expression.
PRINT FEEL: vintage offset newsprint, slight registration misalignment, silkscreen flatness, comic panel punch.

NEGATIVE PROMPT: photorealistic, photograph, 3D render, soft shading, gradients, ambient occlusion, skin pores, film grain, realistic nose, realistic eyes, subtle expression, painterly, airbrush, depth of field, preserved likeness.

Subject: A person seated confidently in the center director's chair of a beachside panel discussion, holding a microphone toward their mouth. Rising directly from their own head, four additional versions of their head are stacked vertically in ascending size, each progressively larger than the one beneath it, balanced like a living totem and gently tilted upward toward the sky. The base head must be rendered at correct, natural human proportion relative to the body — not shrunken or undersized. Each stacked head blends seamlessly and organically into the one below, with hair, skin, and shadow flowing naturally between them so there are no hard edges, no cutout outlines, and no flat composite seams. Every head is posed and angled slightly differently — a subtle turn, a different tilt, a unique expression — so none appear to be a copied duplicate of another.


Wardrobe: A crisp white t-shirt and off-white linen trousers, casual yet business-appropriate in a creative-executive way.


Setting: A sunny coastal panel discussion on a beach, calm turquoise sea and rocky headland behind the subject.


Style: Hyperrealistic and surreal high-end fashion editorial portrait, captured on a clean modern digital medium-format camera, crisp editorial color palette, absurdist luxury realism. Photorealistic detail with dramatic warm sunlit tones and a cinematic low-angle composition that emphasizes the towering, surreal stack. Clean, noise-free image with no film grain, no scratches, no dust, no halation, no vintage texture, no paper or scanned-slide overlay.


Constraints:
- The foreground crowd must be heavily out of focus, softly blurred with a shallow depth of field, reduced to silhouetted heads and shoulders so all sharp focus stays on the subject and the stacked heads.
- Each of the four additional heads must be naturally composited — no awkward cutout outlines, no visible seams, no pasted-on look. Blend skin tone, lighting direction, and shadow so the stack reads as one continuous, organic sculpture.
- Do not repeat the identical head; vary the angle, gaze, and micro-expression of each while preserving the same person's facial features and identity.
- Keep the base head at correct, lifelike proportion to the body; do not make the initial head too small.
- If the subject has long hair, let it flow naturally down and around the head beneath it; never cut the hair off mid-strand.
- Maintain the upward gaze and the stacked, ascending-size arrangement.
- Preserve the low-angle, cinematic composition for the surreal towering effect.
- The final image must be a clean, crisp digital capture — explicitly no grain, no film emulation, no analog texture, no border, no overlay.
- Do not display branding, logos, or text of any kind.
